text:
EXERCISE: DESIGNING ERM AND ERD FOR "SWEET  
HOME"  CONFECTIONERY  STORE  MANAGEMENT  
SYSTEM
1. Context and Business Requirements
The  Sweet  Home confectionery  store  needs  to  build  a  database  to  manage  its  daily  business  
operations. Following a survey, the analysis team collected the following business requirements:
1. Category & Product Management:
• Products  sold  at  the  store  are  categorized  into  different  Categories (e.g.,  
Confectionery, Beverages, Bread, etc.). Each category has a category code and a  
category name. A category can contain multiple products, but each product belongs  
to exactly one category.
• Product information to be stored includes: product code, product name, unit of  
measure (box, packet, bottle, etc.), current selling price, and stock quantity.
2. Employee Management:
• The store has multiple Employees. Each employee has an employee code, full name,  
phone number, hire date, and date of birth.
• The store is divided into different  Positions (e.g., Cashier, Salesperson, Manager,  
etc.). Each position has a position code, position title, and base salary. A position can  
apply to multiple employees, but each employee holds only one position at a time.
3. Customer & Invoice Management:
• Registered  Customers have  a  customer  code,  full  name,  phone  number,  and  
accumulated reward points.
• When  a  customer  makes  a  purchase,  a  cashier  ( Employee)  creates  an  Invoice. 
General invoice information includes: invoice code, creation date and time, and total  
amount.
• Invoice relationship rules:
• An employee can create multiple invoices. Each invoice is created by exactly  
one employee.
• A customer can have multiple invoices. An invoice belongs to exactly one  
customer (if a customer is a walk-in who is not registered, the store assigns a  
default customer code "Guest").
4. Invoice Details Management:
• An invoice can contain multiple products. A product can appear in multiple different  
invoices.

• Business Note: Since this exercise only uses 1-N relationships, students must break  
down the Many-to-Many (N-N) relationship between Invoice and Product into an  
intermediate entity: Invoice Detail.
• Each line in the Invoice Detail records: purchased quantity and selling unit price at  
the time of purchase for a specific product in a specific invoice.
2. Student Requirements
Students are required to complete the task through two main steps:
Step 1: Conceptual Model Design (ERM)
1. Identify all entities in the system.
2. Identify attributes for each entity, clearly classifying:
• Identifiers / Primary Keys.
• Required Attributes (NOT NULL).
• Optional Attributes (NULLABLE).
3. Determine  the  Domain for  each  attribute  in  the  form  of  semantic  descriptions  (e.g.,  
Positive integer, Character string with max length 50, Date, Currency amount, etc.).
4. Draw the ERM diagram  showing entities, attributes, and  1-N relationships along with  
Cardinality / Multiplicity (e.g., 1..1, 0..*, 1..*).
Step 2: Conversion and Logical Model Design (ERD)
1. Convert ERM to ERD : Determine Primary Keys (PK) and Foreign Keys (FK) for the  
tables.
2. Specify Data Types for the ERD corresponding to a popular DBMS (SQL Server, MySQL,  
or PostgreSQL), e.g., INT, V ARCHAR(100), DECIMAL(10,2), DATETIME, etc.
3. Draw  the  complete  ERD  diagram  clearly  displaying  Tables,  PKs,  FKs,  Data  Types,  
Required/Optional constraints, and 1-N relationship lines.
